title: Your study
tomorrow: a pantry wall quotes Jesus. why does it sound so familiar to Amira?

segments.voice: Yesterday, my fasts: chosen, not owed, with a joy waiting at sunset. Today's hunger is a different kind.

A shopping cart, or a wishlist, holding six books on a subject you've just fallen for. A month later, one of them has a bookmark on page twelve. Wanting everything at once is a fast way to finish nothing. So with too many books and one semester, which one do you pick? The Qur'an gives the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ a one-line prayer for exactly this hunger.
screen: `SIX BOOKS IN THE CART.` → `A BOOKMARK ON PAGE TWELVE.` → `A ONE-LINE PRAYER.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in Pickthall's words: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge." Increase. Not: give me all of it by Friday. It's a direction more than a destination: more than yesterday, again tomorrow. A hadith in Sahih Muslim makes the road itself sacred. The Prophet said that whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, God makes easy for them a path to Paradise. A road, walked, step by step. And the Qur'an asks a question that honors anyone on it: "Are those who know equal with those who know not?" So what does ongoing study look like in a real week, with classes or a job already eating the hours? The old picture is a student and a teacher working through one book together, finishing it, then opening the next. Some start with a short classic, like al-Nawawi's Forty Hadith, a hadith at a time. Some take a single surah with a commentary beside it. The pattern holds either way: one book, a regular time for it, and a person to ask when you get stuck, because I don't know needs somewhere to go. One for tonight: the Qur'an's prayer for knowledge asks for more, never for all.
screen: `INCREASE ME IN KNOWLEDGE.` · `A PATH TO PARADISE.` · `THOSE WHO KNOW.` · `ONE BOOK, ONE TIME, ONE PERSON.` · then, large: `MY STUDY.`

segments.voice: Stand up and walk slowly for a minute or two, inside or out. As you walk, ask yourself the one question about faith, or about life, you'd most like answered. Let that question choose your one book.
Your study: your ongoing learning, one book at a time. Its prayer: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
Keep this one: my study, one book and then the next. Seven of ten, still learning.

howItsDone: Muslims who want to keep learning join study circles at mosques, weekend classes or online courses, or read with a teacher, sometimes working through one classic text at a time.

fork.setup: your friend starts a coding course, a language app and a guitar course in the same week. by Sunday she's behind on all three and asks you what to drop. what fits today?
options: keep all three. pushing through is how you grow fastest.
keep one, with a set time and someone to ask, and finish it first.
drop all three until she has a free summer.
fork.reveal: increase, not everything: one book, one time, one person to ask. the road is walked a step at a time.
